title: feat(sharing): ADR-0056 D6 — configurable role-hierarchy widening (role_and_subordinates)
body:
## What (ADR-0056 D6 — configurable role-hierarchy widening)

Role-hierarchy access widening — "a manager sees the records shared with their team" — is now **implemented and configurable per sharing rule**, not the hardcoded no-op the audit found (`Role.parent` was declared but never consumed by any access decision).

**Low-code design (your point — it must be configurable):** this is Salesforce's "grant access using the role hierarchy" expressed *declaratively per rule*, not "managers always see everything":
- A sharing rule declares `recipient_type: 'role_and_subordinates'` (now selectable on `sys_sharing_rule` + in the `SharingRuleRecipientType` contract).
- At evaluation it expands to the named role **plus every subordinate role's users**, by walking the `sys_role.parent` hierarchy via a new **`RoleGraphService`** (mirrors the existing department/team graphs; cycle-safe; system-context lookups).
- Each rule chooses whether to roll up the hierarchy, per object — nothing is hardcoded.

## Verification

- `RoleGraphService` unit tests: downward traversal (incl. self), subordinate-user expansion, **cycle-safe** (A↔B loop terminates), unknown-role → empty.
- `plugin-sharing` full suite **59 tests** green; build clean.

## ADR-0056 status

Done + merged: OWD scenarios (#2062), D4+D8 (#2064), D1+D2 (#2065). **D6** here. Next in the program: D7 default Profile (SSO/JIT foundation), D10 conformance-matrix CI (the durable guardrail), and the release-gated `requireAuth` default flip.

> Note: this lands the configurable *mechanism* + unit proofs. A live end-to-end showcase scenario (rule → materialized `sys_record_share` → manager reads subordinate's record) follows as the next layer.
